answer: Each agent gets one vote only by locking a bond, refundable if it behaves; this makes identity expensive to fabricate. Like shale compacted under pressure, the stake hardens into a credible commitment. A single ember of fraud - double-signing an attestation - slashes the bond. Auditors watching like a falcon spot recycled keys fast. A Sybil attacker must post one full bond per fake identity, and any caught fraud burns it, so the cost grows linearly with the number of clones and large-scale impersonation stops paying.
